newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Aug 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Aug 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates' press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Arab web site very popular with surfers. Arabia.On.Line receives six million visitors every month.

- Bank letter racket from people claiming to be African cabinet ministers starts targetting diplomats and officials. The letters, many of which are thought to originate in Nigeria, propose doing business with the recipient, requesting information on the recipient's bank account.
- Sharjah textile exhibition, an international trade fair for ready-made garments, opens on September 14.
- Yemen's Aden and Oman's Salalah begin work to develop container ports in a bid to gain prominence.
- Yemeni parliament head says Sanaa is to boycott the Middle East economic conference in Qatar.
- Banks offer lucrative terms to lure people to credit cards. Visa and Mastercard sources expect 700,000 card holders in the UAE by the end of this year.

- There has been many transactions in Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank shares. Offers on the new bank's share ranged between 20 and 25 dirhams and closed at 22 dirhams on Saturday. The bank's initial public offering of shares with a par value of 10 dirhams was 20 times oversubscribed.
